What British History PhDs cite, over time

The bibliographies of 1,657 History doctoral dissertations from 16 British universities. Each panel shows the share of a year's dissertations that cite a scholar (any of their works), over a centred three-year window. Shares are normalised by dissertations per year, so corpus growth does not read as rising influence.

Grey line and band: thin windows of fewer than 30 dissertations, mostly before 1990, where one thesis moves the share by several points. The shaded band is a 95% Wilson interval. Years are repository issued years, which can be deposit rather than convocation years. Coverage is by repository holdings and differs by country (coverage-by-university.csv); most dissertations date from after 2010. Trend groups compare 2000–09 with 2018–25 (rising: at least 1.25× and 2 points higher; declining: at most 0.75× and 2 points lower). The final year is a two-year window, and recent deposits may still be incomplete.
